::: {.lead}
Today you plan and rehearse a short talk, as in Lectures 15 and 16. There
are no new ideas. **Part A** is in PowerPoint on the lab computer; **Part
B** is on a simulator of the interactive page: on paper, scan its QR code;
on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its
box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with PowerPoint (the desktop app works best
  for Presenter View).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with PowerPoint.
- **The topic:** *A recycling box in every classroom*, a 3-minute talk for
  your classmates.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · Plan a five-slide talk

**The idea (Lecture 15):** a 3-minute talk needs about five slides, one
idea on each, in this order: **1 Title** › **2 The problem** › **3 The
idea** › **4 An example** (a number or a case) › **5 Thank you and
questions**. Write the speaker notes before you rehearse, and use one quiet
transition on every slide.

**Aim:** plan the five slides of a short talk, with notes.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Make a new presentation with five slides in the order above: slide 1
   and slide 5 with the layout **Title Slide**, slides 2 to 4 with **Title
   and Content**. Give each slide a short title and 2–3 short points.

   {{< record "My five slide titles" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good plan, for example: 1 *A recycling box in every classroom* (your
   name); 2 *The problem* (paper and bottles in the bins); 3 *The idea* (one
   box for paper, one for bottles); 4 *An example* (one class, one week); 5
   *Thank you! Questions?*
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the five slides of a short talk in order.

   1. Title: the topic and your name
   2. The problem
   3. The idea
   4. An example: a number or a case
   5. Thank you and questions

   Why: The audience hears the problem first, then the idea and an example.
   :::

2. Write two sentences of **speaker notes** on slides 2, 3 and 4 (View ›
   Notes): what you will say. Then choose **Transitions › Fade** and click
   **Apply To All**.

   {{< record "My notes for slide 2" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Good notes say more than the slide, in your own words, for example: "Our
   bins are full of paper and bottles. Most of it could be used again." A
   star next to every thumbnail shows the transition.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What goes in the speaker notes?

   - [x] what you will say, in short sentences

     Why: The notes are your reminders; the audience does not see them.

   - [ ] the same points as on the slide

     Why: Notes add what you say, not a copy of the slide.

   - [ ] nothing: you read the slide aloud

     Why: Reading the slide aloud is boring; say more than the slide.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-10/sims/talk-planner.html" poster="../../week-10/sims/talk-planner.png" title="Talk Planner: a five-slide talk" >}}

3. In **Talk Planner**, put Sami's five slides in order and give each one
   its time. How long is the last slide?

   {{< record "The last slide … ; the whole talk …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **At most 30 seconds**: the first and the last slide are short; the
   problem, the idea and the example take the most time. The whole talk is
   about three minutes.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which slide comes right after the title?

   - [x] the problem

     Why: First the audience hears why the talk matters.

   - [ ] the example

     Why: The example comes after the idea.

   - [ ] thank you and questions

     Why: That is the last slide.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Rehearse with Presenter View

**The idea (Lecture 16):** in the slide show, **Presenter View** shows you
the current slide, the next slide, your notes and a **timer**; the audience
sees only the slide. On one screen: start the show, then right-click ›
**Show Presenter View** (or **Alt + F5** in Windows). Rehearse twice, and
watch the timer.

**Aim:** rehearse your talk, and keep it close to its time.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Press **Alt + F5** (or start the show and right-click › **Show Presenter
   View**). Rehearse the talk once, in a low voice, with your notes. Look
   at the timer at the end.

   {{< record "My time … ; what Presenter View shows me …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Presenter View shows **the slide, the next slide, your notes and a
   timer**. A good first time is between two and four minutes; then say
   less, or say your notes fully, and rehearse again.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Presenter View, what does the audience see?

   - [x] only the slide

     Why: The notes, the next slide and the timer are only for the speaker.

   - [ ] the slide and your notes

     Why: The notes stay on your screen.

   - [ ] the timer

     Why: Only the speaker sees the timer.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.html" poster="../../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.png" title="Rehearsal Lab: Presenter View and the timer" >}}

2. In **Rehearsal Lab**, rehearse Sami's talk two times: the first time,
   press Next slide quickly; the second time, keep each slide close to its
   plan. What does the list show the first time?

   {{< record "The first time: … ; the second time: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The first time: **"too short"** for most slides, and a total far below
   3:00. The second time: **"about right"** for every slide, about 3:00 in
   all.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="3:00|3" hint="Add the seconds: 20 + 45 + 45 + 45 + 25."}
   Sami's plan is 0:20, 0:45, 0:45, 0:45 and 0:25. What is the total, in
   minutes?

   Why: 20 + 45 + 45 + 45 + 25 = 180 seconds = 3:00.
   :::
